title: Backfill default autoscaling bounds for existing Dedicated pools (+ dry-run + migration tooling)
author: Michael Nguyen
body:
Context: Dedicated autoscaling now supports per-pool min/max bounds, but existing pools created before the schema change have null/implicit bounds. This PR adds a backfill job + tooling to safely default bounds for existing Dedicated pools without changing behavior unexpectedly, and to provide a dry-run mode for rollout validation. Links ENG-2850.

What this PR does: Adds an idempotent backfill job (control plane) that sets min_replicas/max_replicas on DedicatedPool records where bounds are unset. Defaults are computed from (hardware_class, region, pool_tier) using a centrally versioned table with explicit rationale comments. Adds a CLI entrypoint and admin API endpoint for running the backfill in dry-run mode, outputting a per-pool plan (old -> new bounds, reasons, and any skipped pools). Includes safeguards: (1) never modifies pools with explicit customer-configured bounds, (2) respects multi-region pools by requiring a single hardware_class/region pair or skipping with an actionable reason, (3) clamps defaults to fleet-allowed maxima (per region) to avoid creating unschedulable targets, (4) supports batching + rate limiting to reduce DB load.

Default semantics: This backfill sets defaults as a starting point for the new UX/API fields; it does NOT change autoscaler desired replicas immediately unless/ until bounded enforcement is enabled for that pool via feature flag/allowlist. The defaults are conservative: min defaults to current steady-state replicas when determinable, otherwise to a small region/hardware-specific floor; max defaults to a capped burst ceiling aligned to historical provisioning lead time and regional supply.

Operational tooling: Adds a backfill "plan" report (jsonl) with counts by skip_reason, and a "--dry-run" mode that performs all reads + computations but does not write. Adds a "--since" filter for staged rollouts and a "--pool" filter for targeted remediation. Writes are wrapped in a compare-and-swap guard on updated_at to avoid overwriting concurrent config edits.

Observability/audit: Emits structured events for writes (pool_id, org_id, old_bounds, new_bounds, computed_from, default_table_version) and increments a low-cardinality metric for backfill outcomes (written/skipped/error by reason). Errors are retriable and do not fail the whole run.

Testing: Unit tests for default computation, multi-region skip handling, dry-run output shape, and idempotency; integration test uses a local sqlite fixture to validate CAS behavior. 

Rollout plan: Ship code behind admin-only entrypoints; run dry-run in prod for all pools; review report with Fleet/SRE; then run writes for allowlisted cohorts by region (us-east-1 -> eu-west-1 -> ap-southeast-1).
commits: control-plane: add default bounds table + computation helper
control-plane: implement DedicatedPoolBoundsBackfill job with dry-run support
admin: add CLI entrypoint for backfill run + plan export
observability: add outcome metrics + structured audit events for backfill writes
tests: idempotency + CAS guard + multi-region skip coverage
docs: operator notes for staged runs and expected skip reasons
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Can you clarify how we avoid overwriting a customer update if they set bounds while the job is running? Also want to ensure multi-region pools don’t get partially updated.

Michael Nguyen (author): Added CAS guard on updated_at + explicit check for bounds fields still null inside the transaction. Multi-region pools are treated as atomic: if >1 region or mixed hardware_class, we skip entirely with reason=multi_region_unsupported_for_backfill (no partial writes).
Vanessa Ortiz (review): Default max=8 for h100 in us-east-1 seems high given current supply. Can we clamp to fleet regional cap and make that explicit in the plan output?

Michael Nguyen (author): Yep—now clamps computed max to FleetAllowedMax[region][hardware_class] and includes {"clamped":true,"clamp_reason":"fleet_regional_cap"} in the plan output. Also added a histogram-free counter by clamp_reason only.
Aisha Bello (review): Please ensure metrics are low-cardinality. org_id/pool_id should not appear in metrics labels. Events are fine but metrics need strict label set.
Michael Nguyen (author): Adjusted: metric labels are now {outcome, reason, region, hardware_class} with region/hardware_class capped to our known enums. org_id/pool_id only in structured logs/events.

Jordan Lee (review): One concern: setting min defaults based on current replicas could effectively encode a transient overprovisioning state. Do we have a threshold to avoid locking in an incident spike?

Michael Nguyen (author): Good point. Updated logic: min defaults to p50 of last 7 days applied_replicas (if available); falls back to current replicas only when telemetry missing. Also caps min at (recommended_floor + 2) unless pool has a pinned min already (which we don’t touch). Added tests for the "incident spike" case using a synthetic time series.
Benji Okafor (approval): LGTM after the CAS + telemetry-based min change. Please coordinate dry-run output review with SRE before any writes in prod.
Michael Nguyen (author): Will do. Follow-up task in ENG-2850 to attach dry-run report to the rollout checklist.
release_notes: Internal/admin-only: Adds tooling to backfill default autoscaling min/max bounds for existing Dedicated pools, including dry-run planning and safe, idempotent writes.
final_status: Merged to main. Rollout requires admin execution; no customer-visible change until bounded enforcement is enabled per pool via feature flag/allowlist.
